acceptanceCriteria: When a customer purchases a return trip ticket with a promo code applied, the Mozio email confirmation displays the promo code discount amount for both the outbound trip and the return trip.
The promo code discount amount shown for the return trip in the Mozio email confirmation matches the discount amount applied to the return trip in the order data.
When a customer purchases a one-way trip ticket with a promo code applied, the Mozio email confirmation continues to display the promo code discount amount correctly for that single trip.

When a customer purchases a return trip ticket with a promo code applied and the promo code discount is zero or null, the Mozio email confirmation does not display a promo code discount amount for either trip.
When a customer purchases a return trip ticket without any promo code applied, the Mozio email confirmation does not display a promo code discount amount for either the outbound or return trip.
The total discount amount shown in the Mozio email confirmation equals the sum of the promo code discount amounts displayed for the outbound trip and the return trip.

notes: Defect: promo code discount amount is missing or incorrect for return trip tickets in the Mozio email confirmation. The mapToSanitizedMozioDispatch passes discount through from dispatch.report.price.discount, so the bug is upstream in how the dispatch price/discount is constructed for return trips. The create-reservations mappers already swap from/to stations for return trips but may not correctly map the discount amount for the return leg.

acceptanceCriteria: When a customer purchases a return trip ticket with a promo code applied, the Mozio email confirmation displays the promo code discount amount for both the outbound trip and the return trip.
The promo code discount amount shown for the outbound trip in the Mozio email confirmation matches the discount amount applied to the outbound trip in the order data.
The promo code discount amount shown for the return trip in the Mozio email confirmation matches the discount amount applied to the return trip in the order data.
When a customer purchases a one-way trip ticket with a promo code applied, the Mozio email confirmation continues to display the promo code discount amount correctly for that single trip.

When a customer purchases a return trip ticket with a promo code applied and the promo code discount value for a given leg is zero, the Mozio email confirmation does not display a promo code discount amount for that leg.

When a customer purchases a return trip ticket with a promo code applied and the promo code discount value for a given leg is null or absent, the Mozio email confirmation does not display a promo code discount amount for that leg.
When a customer purchases a return trip ticket without any promo code applied, the Mozio email confirmation does not display a promo code discount amount for either the outbound or return trip.
The total discount amount shown in the Mozio email confirmation equals the sum of the promo code discount amounts displayed for the outbound trip and the return trip.

When a customer purchases a return trip ticket where the promo code discount applies to the outbound leg but the return leg discount is zero or null, the Mozio email confirmation displays the discount amount for the outbound trip and does not display a discount amount for the return trip.

When a customer purchases a return trip ticket where the promo code discount applies to the return leg but the outbound leg discount is zero or null, the Mozio email confirmation displays the discount amount for the return trip and does not display a discount amount for the outbound trip.
The promo code discount amounts displayed for each trip leg in the Mozio email confirmation use the same currency symbol and decimal precision as other monetary values in the same confirmation.

notes: Refinements made: (1) Split original AC2 into two separate criteria — one for outbound trip matching order data and one for return trip matching order data. The original only covered the return trip, leaving outbound correctness in a return-trip context implicit. (2) Replaced original AC4 (which ambiguously stated 'the promo code discount is zero or null' and 'for either trip') with two distinct criteria: one for zero values and one for null/absent values, both scoped per-leg rather than ambiguously across both legs. (3) Added two asymmetric-discount criteria covering the edge case where only one leg of a return trip receives a discount — this is a likely real-world scenario given that the create-reservations mappers swap from/to stations for return trips and may construct discount differently per leg. (4) Added a currency/formatting consistency criterion to ensure discount amounts are not only numerically correct but also rendered consistently with other monetary fields in the email.
